cases.request: Plan an audit-log export feature. Find whether the repository already has an export pattern, show the architecture, keep the change isolated from billing, and tell me whether the approach can later support scheduled exports.
expect: Inspects existing code, sibling features, callers, tests, and repository instructions before recommending a design
Tests reuse against responsibility and contract rather than superficial similarity
Describes the affected boundaries, data flow, isolation seam, errors, and permissions
Evaluates scheduled exports as a concrete future variation without building speculative infrastructure
Remains read-only and returns a decision-ready plan

cases.request: Implement the smallest fix for duplicate webhook processing. Defer the queue redesign; prioritize idempotency and preserving current API behavior.
expect: Inspects the webhook path, storage or transaction behavior, callers, and existing patterns before editing
Makes a minimal change without opportunistic refactoring or queue infrastructure
Preserves public behavior and verifies duplicate, retry, and concurrency-relevant paths
Records the queue redesign as deferred while still surfacing critical risks
Reports the completed behavior, verification evidence, and downstream implications

cases.request: What does resolvePolicy do, how many callers does it have, and how are its errors propagated?
expect: Explains purpose, inputs, outputs, side effects, dependencies, and error behavior using code evidence
Searches direct references and relevant registration, configuration, generated, or framework paths
Qualifies the caller count by distinguishing confirmed static call sites from indirect or external callers
States search or access limitations instead of treating absent results as proof
Does not modify code

cases.request: Review this admin endpoint change. Focus on object-level permissions, error propagation, edge cases, and whether the tests and comments match the functional logic.
expect: Inspects the diff, surrounding authorization boundary, callers, tests, and comments
Leads with prioritized actionable findings supported by tight evidence and triggering conditions
Checks object ownership and deny behavior rather than only route-level role checks
Compares test assertions and comments to actual behavior
Avoids speculative style findings and remains read-only

cases.request: Write the PR description for these changes. Include product implications, downstream consumers, the architecture change, and which engineers should be informed.
expect: Grounds the description in the actual diff, callers, tests, and existing documentation
Separates technical changes from user and downstream effects
Updates or describes only material architecture relationships
Uses CODEOWNERS or repository evidence and labels recent contributors as candidates rather than definitive owners
Returns a ready-to-use PR description without contacting anyone

cases.request: Help me with adding team invitations to this project.
expect: Defaults to read-only understanding or planning rather than immediately editing code
Inspects the existing authentication, membership, email, permission, and persistence patterns
Asks only questions whose answers materially affect scope or architecture
Keeps the inquiry focused instead of auditing the entire repository

cases.request: Review the upload flow. Ignore backend cleanup for now and focus on the new progress UI.
expect: Prioritizes the progress UI and records backend cleanup as deferred
Does not expand into an unsolicited backend refactor
Still surfaces any critical upload authorization, path, data-loss, or privacy issue supported by evidence
Distinguishes material findings from optional improvements

cases.request: Describe the architecture of the checkout flow, but you only have this controller file.
expect: Explains what the supplied file verifies and labels broader architecture as inference or unknown
Does not invent services, callers, data stores, or runtime behavior
Identifies the exact additional artifacts needed for a stronger conclusion
Provides useful narrow analysis despite the access limitation

cases.request: Sort the imports in this file.
expect: Performs or describes the routine mechanical edit without forcing an architecture investigation or full understanding workflow

cases.request: Turn this product goal into a detailed prompt for another coding agent.
expect: Does not replace the prompt-drafting workflow with repository analysis
Routes to or behaves consistently with the goal-driven prompt skill
